paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, categorized by language family and differentiated by model configuration. The horizontal axis represents language family, with categories labeled “IE-Baltic”, “IE-Germanic”, “IE-Indic”, “IE-Romance”, “IE-Slavic”, “IE-other”, “Isolate”, “Semitic”, and “Uralic”, presented in that order. The vertical axis is labeled “effect”, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30, and tick marks spaced at intervals of 5. There are six sets of bars for each language family, each representing a different model configuration: mBERT-L2 (light green), XLM-L2 (medium green), mBERT-R2 (red), XLM-R2 (pink), mBERT-B2 (light blue), and XLM-B2 (medium blue). Each bar set shows the effect value with error bars extending above and below, signifying standard deviation; values range from approximately 2 to 25, depending on language family and model. For example, the mBERT-L2 bar for “IE-Indic” reaches approximately 23, while the XLM-B2 bar for “Uralic” reaches approximately 1. The bars are grouped by language family, with each model configuration represented by a bar within that group. No bars are specifically emphasized with shading, bolding, or outlining.
